newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says rice imports will prevent shortfall.
newsitem.headline: Manila says rice imports will prevent shortfall.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday he had approved the early imports of rice this year to ensure enough supply of the staple during the traditionally lean months of July and August.

"The National Food Authority upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Agriculture and approval of the President has decided to do the necessary rice imports earlier compared to 1995 and 1996," Ramos said at his weekly news conference.

Earlier this month, Agriculture Department officials said the NFA has been authorised by Ramos to import up to 650,000 tonnes of rice from neighbouring countries before the onset of the lean months, which start in July.
Philippine rice output is traditionally low in the third quarter.
Agriculture Department officials said the NFA has clinched deals to buy up to 200,000 tonnes of rice each from Vietnam and China and up to 205,000 tonnes from Thailand.
Ramos said the government is doing its best to increase the productivity of rice farms by extending credit and technical assistance to farmers.
More funds are also being allocated for post-harvest facilities and farm to market roads, he said.
Ramos also said his administration will push Congress to approve a bill to increase funds for irrigation facilities to further boost domestic rice harvests.
